lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Does [Promise.all|Promise dot all] cancel the other promises when one of them fails?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: No. It only rejects right away. The other promises keep running.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Three tasks. A takes three hundred milliseconds, one fails after one hundred, and C takes two hundred.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: At one hundred, [Promise.all|Promise dot all] rejects, and we print rejected.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: But look. C and A still finish afterward. Nothing was cancelled.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: Why can it not cancel them?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: A promise has no cancel method. It only represents a result that will arrive.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Cancelling means stopping the work behind the promise, and that is up to the work itself.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: The standard tool is [AbortController|abort controller]. Give every task the same signal.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: When one fails, call abort, and each task can stop its own work.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Now only rejected is printed. A and C never finish.

lines.speaker: sam
lines.text: And if I want to wait for everything?

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Use [Promise.allSettled|Promise dot all settled]. It never rejects, and it reports every result.

lines.speaker: byte
lines.text: Remember: [Promise.all|Promise dot all] combines results. It does not cancel work.
